title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
description: The engine control module has detected a misfire in cylinder 1.
solutions: Check spark plug
Check ignition coil
Inspect fuel injector
Check compression

title: Camshaft Timing Over-Advanced, Bank 1
description: The Engine Control Module (ECM) has determined that the Bank 1 camshaft timing is more advanced than what the ECM has commanded.
solutions: Check and top up engine oil
Perform an oil and filter change
Inspect and replace VVT solenoid
Check timing chain alignment

title: Mass Air Flow Circuit Low
description: The Mass Air Flow (MAF) sensor output voltage to the ECM is lower than the expected standard range.
possibleCauses: Wiring or connector issue in the MAF circuit
solutions: Clean the MAF sensor
Check for and repair vacuum leaks
Inspect wiring and connectors
Replace the MAF sensor

title: Coolant Below Thermostat Temperature
description: The engine is not reaching its optimal operating temperature within the expected amount of time.
solutions: Replace the engine thermostat
Check and fill coolant to the proper level
Test or replace the ECT sensor
Inspect cooling fan operation

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit, Bank 1 Sensor 1
description: The ECM has detected a malfunction in the heater circuit of the upstream oxygen sensor on Bank 1.
possibleCauses: Poor electrical connection or damaged wiring
solutions: Replace Bank 1 Sensor 1 oxygen sensor
Check and replace related fuses
Inspect and repair wiring harness
Test circuit for proper voltage and ground

title: System Too Lean, Bank 1
description: The engine is running with too much air and not enough fuel (lean condition) in Bank 1.
possibleCauses: Vacuum leak in the intake manifold or hoses
Faulty or dirty Mass Air Flow (MAF) sensor
Low fuel pressure (weak pump, clogged filter)
solutions: Perform a smoke test to find vacuum leaks
Clean or replace MAF sensor
Check fuel pressure and replace fuel filter if needed
Inspect exhaust system for leaks before the O2 sensor

title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire
description: The ECM has detected misfires occurring randomly across multiple cylinders, rather than being isolated to a specific one.
possibleCauses: Worn spark plugs or bad ignition coils
Low fuel pressure or poor fuel quality
Faulty EGR valve or MAF sensor
solutions: Inspect and replace spark plugs/coils
Check for vacuum leaks
Test fuel pressure
Clean fuel injectors and check fuel quality

title: EGR Flow Insufficient
description: The Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) system is not flowing enough exhaust gas back into the intake manifold.
solutions: Clean EGR valve and intake passages
Check and replace DPFE sensor if faulty
Inspect and replace damaged vacuum lines
Test EGR solenoid operation

title: Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold, Bank 1
description: The catalytic converter on Bank 1 is not operating efficiently and failing to properly clean the exhaust emissions.
possibleCauses: Exhaust leak before or near the catalytic converter
Engine misfires causing raw fuel to enter the exhaust
solutions: Fix any existing misfire or rich/lean codes first
Check for and repair exhaust leaks
Test or replace the downstream O2 sensor
Replace the catalytic converter

title: Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold, Bank 2
description: The catalytic converter on Bank 2 is not operating efficiently and failing to properly clean the exhaust emissions.
possibleCauses: Exhaust leak near the Bank 2 converter
solutions: Fix any existing engine performance codes first
Check for and repair exhaust leaks
Test or replace the Bank 2 downstream O2 sensor
Replace the Bank 2 catalytic converter

title: EVAP System Small Leak
description: The Evaporative Emission Control (EVAP) system has detected a small vapor leak in the fuel system.
possibleCauses: Loose, damaged, or missing gas cap
Small leak in an EVAP hose or line
Faulty purge valve or vent solenoid
solutions: Tighten or replace the gas cap
Perform a smoke test on the EVAP system
Test and replace purge or vent solenoids
Inspect charcoal canister for cracks

title: EVAP System Large Leak
description: The Evaporative Emission Control (EVAP) system has detected a large vapor leak or lack of purge flow.
possibleCauses: Gas cap left off or severely damaged
solutions: Check and tighten/replace gas cap
Visually inspect EVAP hoses for disconnections
Test the EVAP vent valve
Smoke test system to pinpoint large leaks

title: Idle Control System Malfunction
description: The ECM is unable to maintain or control the engine idle speed properly.
possibleCauses: Carbon buildup in the throttle body
solutions: Clean the throttle body and IAC passages
Test or replace the IAC valve
Check for and repair vacuum leaks
Inspect air intake system
